publicationStmt.p: Working authority file for the Digital Corpus of Armenian Colophons. Publication details and licensing will be established for the corpus.

sourceDesc.p: Place records will be compiled from reviewed colophon witnesses, historical geography, and supporting scholarship. Each identification will retain its supporting evidence. Nine initial records correspond to the two test colophons and their manuscript descriptions.

projectDesc.p: This file records geographical entities referenced across the corpus, including settlements, regions, and monastic sites. Claims that a manuscript was copied, owned, or used at a place remain in the relevant colophon files.

editorialDecl.p: Place identifiers follow the pattern place-000001. Allocate each identifier once and retain it when names, classifications, or geographical identifications change.

Use placeName elements for preferred names and attested variants, including Armenian and transliterated forms where available. Record modern names separately and only when the identification is supported. The values preferred, variant, and modern on placeName/@type are project conventions. The exact form found in a witness remains in its transcription.

Use place/@type for the geographical category. Initial candidate values are settlement, region, monastery, church, and site; these are documented here and will be refined through actual corpus cases. They describe the place, not its role in a colophon. A monastic site and the community occupying it are distinct entities.

Use location for geographical information. Distinguish historical geographical context from modern administrative location. References to other place records in this file use a local fragment such as #place-000002. Do not infer historical boundaries from modern administrative divisions.

Coordinates are desired where available. Use geo with WGS84 decimal-degree coordinates in latitude longitude order. Document the coordinate source, uncertainty, and whether the point represents a known site or an approximate centre. A point for a region does not describe its extent. Omit coordinates for unlocated places; do not substitute zero values.

Use note elements for identification and uncertainty, bibl elements for supporting references, and idno elements for verified external identifiers. Bibliographical references point to listbibl.xml with the appropriate record fragment.

revisionDesc.change: Added nine place records, including Sebasteia and the user-confirmed identification of Harput, with maximum example fields in the first three entries.

place.placeName: Eranšahr
place.note: The historical region named in the editorial note explaining the use of Aryan in Colophon 1. Its historical scope is to be documented separately from modern administrative boundaries.
Referenced in Colophon 1.

place.placeName: Church of Saint Peter, Antioch
place.note: The church named in the account of the celebration following victory at Antioch in Colophon 1. The record identifies the church as referred to in the text; its precise site remains to be established.
Referenced in Colophon 1.

place.placeName: Melitene
place.note: The settlement named as the place of translation in Colophon 2, dated 1092.
Referenced in Colophon 2.

place.placeName: Harput
Elâzig
place.note: The production place supplied for Venice, Mekhitarist monastery of San Lazzaro MS. 17, dated 1224. Lewis Read confirms that the label Elâzig in the manuscript description refers here to Harput.
Recorded in the description of Venice, Mekhitarist monastery of San Lazzaro MS. 17.
